| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | not-started | 2026-08-03 — D38 recorded, amending D2, D7 and D23 — a module declares a version again, supplied by a catalog-style identity SUBPACKAGE exporting both ModulePath and Version. Recorded while walking 0011's Open Questions, where the command-surface half lands as 0011 D12; the two are contingent on each other. WHAT REOPENED D2 was a consumer this entry had not accounted for, found by measurement rather than by argument: an instance derives its version from the module and declares NONE OF ITS OWN (library/opm/module/instance.go:110's ModuleVersion(); core/src/module_instance.cue), and core/src/transformer.cue:105 declares `version: string` NON-OPTIONALLY inside #moduleInstanceMetadata. Under D2 a registry-acquired module could have that field filled from the resolved coordinate, but a module rendered FROM DISK has no coordinate — which is D2's OWN stated reason for rejecting its second alternative, that `a module read from disk has no identity`. 0010 never named transformer.cue:101-109 in its edit surface and never said what supplies the field after the deletion, so the entry carried an unfilled declaration it had not noticed. Recorded so the case is not overstated: measured 2026-08-03, NO SHIPPED TRANSFORMER READS `.version` — 117 uses of #moduleInstanceMetadata across catalog_opm, catalog_kubernetes and catalog_opm_experimental, every one of them .name or .namespace — so nothing breaks either way and the choice is about which design leaves a declared field with no filler. THE INVARIANT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT MAKES THIS SAFE, and it is stated everywhere a reader could meet the field rather than only in the decision. D2's deletion rested on two reasons; the drift reason is answered by 0011 D12's publish assertion, and the second — that fqn interpolated version, so a moving version moved module.uuid -> instance.uuid -> the owner label on every resource, after which prune.go:107 skipped every delete WHILE REPORTING SUCCESS — was removed independently by D1 making fqn the module path. So the field returns barred from fqn and uuid, and wiring it back into either restores a silent orphaning that emits no Event, no status field and no metric. That is now a first-class RISK in 05-risks rather than a comment, a MUST-FAIL case in schemas/target.cue (_moduleFqnLeak, confirmed 2026-08-03 against cue v0.17.1 — and it fails STRUCTURALLY on `fqn: conflicting values` before the regex ever runs, because fqn: #ModulePathType & modulePath admits no other value), and an accepted->implemented gate requiring a test that asserts changing only `version` moves NEITHER fqn NOR uuid — both, because a test checking fqn alone will not catch a uuid regression. D7 IS PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED, NOT REVERSED: its measurement stands and is why the subpackage is the shape — a top-level field beside the embedded #Module in the ROOT package still fails at re-unification with `field not allowed`, vetting clean standalone. A separate package is never unified into #Module, so it avoids the failure entirely. D23 IS REVERSED: it kept the two artifact types at different placements on the reasoning that the module half of the writer `has nothing to decide` under D2, which restoring the version removes; its self-import cost is real and unchanged, but `opm module init` generates the import so the cost lands on a template rather than on every module author. DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED: whether D11's read-side check extends to comparing an acquired module's metadata.version against the tag it was fetched by. D2 had made that comparison impossible and D38 makes it available; doing it would close the drift for artifacts published outside `opm publish`, not doing it keeps D11 about the address alone. #FetchedArtifact's comment records the choice as open rather than silently keeping today's behaviour. Narrative surface corrected across 02-design (design point 2, the core/src/module.cue and shape.go edit lines, the SPEC.md :252-256 range), 06-operational (Semver Impact and the deprecation table, whose row now reads NOT REMOVED), 04-graduation (the modules/ gate now requires identity/identity.cue with both constants), README's cross-reference table (gaining transformer.cue:105 and instance.go:110 as the consumers that forced this), and 05-risks, where the `#Catalog and #Module stop being symmetric` drawback is RETIRED — both now carry a version, and what remains is an asymmetry of MEANING that is worth stating precisely because it is invisible: a catalog's version keys its transformers and stamps provenance, so changing it moves keys, while a module's keys nothing at all. | Module and Catalog Identity |
| [0011](./0011/) | cli | draft | minor | not-started | 2026-08-03 — OQ walk, session 1: D10, D11 and D12 recorded; OQ1, OQ2, OQ3 and OQ8 RESOLVED. Both questions 04-graduation declared BLOCKING are now closed, and five remain — OQ4, OQ5, OQ6, OQ7, OQ9. Walked in dependency order rather than numeric order, because OQ3 gates OQ4's candidate (b) and OQ7/OQ9 both decide what OQ6's migration rewrites. D10 (OQ3) makes published artifacts IMMUTABLE by registry enforcement, researched rather than assumed: Zot has NO immutability flag and the documented mechanism is withholding the `update` authorization action, with create/update distinguished PER TAG rather than per repository (pkg/api/authz.go upgrades CreatePermission to UpdatePermission only when the reference already appears in the repo's tag list) — which is what makes it usable for a catalog shipping many releases, since a read+create policy that gated per REPOSITORY would allow exactly one tag. The author's initial namespace asymmetry (catalogs strict, modules relaxed) was dropped once the registry turned out to be MULTI-TENANT with arbitrary tenant paths: there is no path predicate to scope on, so `**/catalogs/**` would be a guess about another tenant's layout. Two independent objections are recorded anyway — nothing in the normal flow needs `update`, since every -dev and -e2e.g<sha> tag is a NEW tag and therefore a create; and a ModuleInstance pins spec.module.{path,version}, so a mutable module tag moves rendered bytes under an instance whose source did not change, making the exposure differ in DEGREE, which is the test D6 itself set when it justified its own module/catalog split as differing in KIND. Maven-style no-deletion was rejected on a counter-example from this workspace: the opm_experimental canonicalisation on 2026-07-31 REQUIRED deleting a repository in two registries, and localhost:5000's registry:2 refused with 405 because deletes were disabled, forcing an on-disk removal. Delete is therefore withheld from the default policy and retained by an administrator, which is inherent in operating the storage rather than a permission this design grants. GHCR CANNOT DO ANY OF THIS — community discussion #181783 is open and unanswered since 2025-12-12 — and that is accepted deliberately: the requirement takes effect when a conforming registry exists, with no urgency to get there. D10 was REFRAMED the same day on the author's scope note that these entries define how OPM WORKS WITH a future central registry rather than specifying one: it now binds a CLASS rather than a host, because the Zot configuration ships as an open module so there is a reference configuration and N deployments, and the Zot policy is labelled demonstrated feasibility rather than deployment specification. D11 (OQ2) gives the CLI `opm login [registry]`, resolving its target through the EXISTING ResolveRegistry precedence (flag > OPM_REGISTRY > config.registry in ~/.opm/config.cue) so pointing OPM at another deployment needs no new surface — which is what makes the open module usable rather than nominal. Credentials land in a store CUE ALREADY READS, and that is mechanical rather than preferential: CUE performs the push, so a credential written anywhere else is invisible at the moment it is needed. Measured from cue v0.17.1 — `cue login --help` directs users to `docker login`/`podman login` for any non-Central registry and reads what they write — so an OPM-private store is EXCLUDED rather than deferred, while a docker-credential-opm helper stays available as the upgrade path since helpers keep one store rather than adding a second. The authentication MECHANISM (htpasswd, LDAP, OIDC social login, API keys, mTLS, OIDC workload identity for CI) is left to the rollout by agreement. Recorded because it bears on the migration: opm-operator/cmd/main.go's resolveRegistry documents a flag > env > default precedence but gives the flag a NON-EMPTY compiled-in default, so OPM_REGISTRY is inert on the operator; the CLI's flag defaults to empty and its precedence works, and it already reports shadowed values — so a Zot cutover repoints the CLI by config and needs a code change for the operator. D12 (OQ1 + OQ8) is the largest and reverses this entry's direction on the module side. Modules gain a catalog-style identity SUBPACKAGE exporting both ModulePath and Version, `opm module version set` exists, and `--version` means ONE thing on both commands — fill an open field, ASSERT a concrete one, refuse on mismatch — writing the WORKING TREE rather than a copy, since a copy is the only candidate that guarantees the published bytes exist in no commit and D10 makes each instance permanent. The trigger was the author asking why modules had no `version set`; the answer was that 0010 D2 deleted the field, and walking that back surfaced an unfilled declaration in 0010 (transformer.cue:105) which is now 0010 D38. Publish additionally verifies metadata.version == id.Version because core CANNOT enforce the wiring — #Module has no way to reference an arbitrary module's identity package — so the template establishes the derivation, CUE enforces it for free while it is written (`conflicting values` at vet), and the publish check exists solely for the author who REPLACES id.Version with a literal and leaves nothing to conflict with. schemas/target.cue gained #IdentityState's assert half and a new #IdentityDerivation, both MUST-FAIL cases confirmed 2026-08-03 against cue v0.17.1 (_asserted and agrees each yielding `conflicting values false and true`). D12 is CONTINGENT on 0010 D38 landing; the two were written together and neither describes a workable shape alone. | Module and Catalog Publishing |

| [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |
| [0014](./0014/) | cli | draft | none | not-started | 2026-07-29 — Drafted. 0006 shipped the handoff that moves an instance's manager to the operator; nothing moves its definition out of the cluster, so a CLI-first user who now wants GitOps hand-assembles four YAML documents per instance from a `kubectl get -o yaml` dump. Three decisions came from the user on the day: the exported unit is the CR plus its apply envelope rather than a bare CR (D1), export refuses to write unless the published module reproduces `status.lastAppliedRenderDigest` (D2, reusing handoff's gate chain and `VerificationDigest`), and `spec.values` is written verbatim with a warning rather than redacted or refused, because OPM cannot yet identify which values are secret (D3). D4 records the live CR as the sole input. Two findings from reading the code shaped the design. `ApplySpec` (cli/internal/inventory/store.go:119) writes only `spec.module`, `spec.owner`, and `spec.values`, so every CLI-written CR lacks `spec.serviceAccountName` and `spec.prune` — meaning a dump-and-strip export applies under the controller's own identity and orphans its workloads on delete, a behaviour difference invisible in the YAML. And the render-bearing / apply-bearing partition resolves the tension that finding creates: the fields the digest gate verifies are copied untouched, while the fields governing apply identity and deletion sit outside the render digest and can be completed without weakening the guarantee, provided every completion is reported. The partition is enforced in schemas/target.cue rather than asserted in prose. Six open questions; OQ4 (field-manager collision when Flux's kustomize-controller applies over fields owned by opm-cli and the operator) is the load-bearing one and is gated on a runnable experiment, because it decides whether the adoption is as quiet as D2's guarantee implies. | Export a Deployed Instance as GitOps Manifests |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
